name: badusb-remote-desktop
description: Flipper Zero BadUSB payloads that make a fresh, keyboard-less machine reachable on the LAN for remote desktop — macOS Screen Sharing (VNC), Windows RDP, Linux VNC.

readme.html:
badusb-remote-desktop

Plug a Flipper Zero into a brand-new computer and it sets itself up for remote desktop — no keyboard or mouse needed. The machine even says its own IP out loud when it's done.

  ┌─────────────┐   USB    ┌──────────────┐   "my address    ┌──────────┐
  │ Flipper Zero │ ───────▶ │ new computer │ ──── is ... " ──▶│ your eyes │
  │  (BadUSB)    │  types   │  (no kb/ms)  │   spoken aloud   │  + laptop │
  └─────────────┘ commands └──────────────┘                  └──────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼  reachable on the LAN
                          vnc://<ip>:5900  ·  rdp://<ip>

When to use this

You just got a new machine and want to drive it from your laptop — but you don't want to dig out a spare keyboard, mouse, and monitor just to switch on remote access.

  • ✅ Use it for: setting up your own Macs, PCs, and Linux boxes as you get them.
  • 🚫 Don't use it for: hardware that isn't yours, or air-gapped machines (these need a network).

Why a BadUSB?

A fresh machine has no remote access yet — that's the chicken-and-egg problem. The Flipper pretends to be a keyboard and types the setup for you, so you need zero peripherals and the same payload works on every new box.

How

  1. Edit the password(s) in your OS's payload — replace each CHANGE_ME_*. Save it as *.local.txt (gitignored) so secrets stay out of git.
  2. Copy the payload to the Flipper SD card → badusb/ folder.
  3. Boot the target to its desktop, signed in as admin, on a network.
  4. Run it: plug in the Flipper → BadUSB app → pick the payload → Run.
  5. Listen — it announces its IP. Connect from your laptop. ⬇️

Pick your payload

TargetPayloadTurns onConnect with
macOSpayloads/macos-enable-vnc.txtScreen Sharing (VNC) + SSHVNC client :5900
Windowspayloads/windows-enable-rdp.txtRemote Desktop (RDP)RDP client
Windowspayloads/windows-enable-ssh.txtOpenSSH Server (sshd) port 22ssh <user>@<ip>
Windows (passwordless)payloads/windows-push-ssh-key.txtinstalls your SSH public keyssh <user>@<ip>
Debian/Ubuntu (GNOME)payloads/linux-gnome-enable-vnc.txtgnome-remote-desktop (VNC)VNC client :5900
Debian/Ubuntu (X11)scripts/linux-x11vnc-fallback.shx11vnc + systemd serviceVNC client :5900

Connect in

VNC (macOS + Linux) → port 5900:

open vnc://<ip>:5900     # macOS Screen Sharing.app — or RealVNC / TigerVNC / Remmina

RDP (Windows):

  • macOS: free Windows App → Add PC → <ip>
  • Linux: xfreerdp /v:<ip> /u:<user> — or Remmina

⚠️ Before you run one

  • Needs a network. Payloads type the commands inline (no curl|bash), but the target still has to be online — that's the whole point.
  • Passwords get baked in. A keyboardless box can't have you type at the prompt, so the payload types the password for you. It lives in plaintext on the SD card while it's there → save edited copies as *.local.txt and wipe the card after if you care.
  • VNC passwords max out at 8 characters (a VNC-protocol limit). Longer = silently truncated.
  • Set the Flipper keyboard layout to US — the payloads assume US-layout symbols.

Gotchas by OS

macOS — uses kickstart to enable legacy VNC + SSH; answers one sudo prompt. If a VNC client won't authenticate on Sonoma/Sequoia, set the password once via System Settings → General → Sharing → Screen Sharing (everything else stays put).

Windows — gets RDP, not VNC (Windows has no built-in VNC server; adding one needs an installer = a future stager payload). RDP only works for accounts with a password. The UAC "Yes" step uses the US Alt+Y accelerator.

Windows (SSH) — windows-enable-ssh.txt installs the OpenSSH Server capability (needs the box online — it pulls from Windows Update; bump the DELAY after the install step on a slow link) and opens port 22. For passwordless login, windows-push-ssh-key.txt writes your key to C:\ProgramData\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys — admin accounts use that file, not ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, and sshd rejects it unless the ACL is locked to SYSTEM + Administrators (the payload does this with icacls). Edit in your public key and save as windows-push-ssh-key.local.txt first.

Linux — primary payload uses grdctl, which works under Wayland (where x11vnc doesn't). Needs a logged-in GNOME session. On GNOME 46+ the grdctl vnc commands may differ — if it errors, run scripts/linux-x11vnc-fallback.sh on the box instead.

Timing — every payload front-loads DELAYs for app launches. On a slow/cold boot, bump the DELAY after whichever step ran too early.

Roadmap

  • VNC-on-Windows via a stager (silent TightVNC/TigerVNC install)
  • Fedora (dnf) and Arch (pacman) variants
  • Optional Tailscale enrollment → reachable off-LAN too
  • DEFINE-based password templating instead of CHANGE_ME hand-edits

Security & scope

Provisioning automation for machines you own and physically control. It enables remote-desktop services and types credentials you supply — don't point it at hardware that isn't yours, and treat the SD card like it holds your passwords (while a *.local.txt is on it, it does).

License
